title: Use shared BVH candidates and batch coupling work
requires: Production shared runtime/Slang toolchain and an applicable physical GPU; cross-adapter build coverage
scope: Audit every currently supported production coupling consumer, replace remaining all-endpoint/all-triangle searches with complete candidates from the single published dynamic BVH, and batch compatible edge/endpoint dispatches. Include the soft-body/cloth full-triangle scan and per-record attachment kernels identified at 75584181. Follow docs/roadmap/F8-DISPATCH-REDUCTION.md and docs/roadmap/F8-SINGLE-EXECUTION-PATH.md.
acceptance: Map each supported pair/mode to its production search, candidate buffers and dispatch graph. Mechanical/proximity interactions consume generation-tagged common-epoch candidates; explicit attachments use their known endpoint identities, and regular-grid stencil operations retain their documented grid algorithm without an unnecessary BVH query.

Remove unconditional per-node scans of every opposing triangle/body and full candidate regeneration in each solve sweep. Candidate completeness follows the full-tick swept/correction envelope and passes independent brute-force oracle checks for thin crossings, sparse resources, mixed families and topology/endpoint replacement.

Batch compatible graph edges/attachment records so adding same-mode edges increases device work rather than reproducing a host kernel sequence per record. Record independent numerical dispatch and candidate/narrow-phase work ceilings for fixed sparse/dense scaling fixtures before optimization; include negative controls that reject the audited brute-force/per-record implementation.

Reuse one dynamic spatial build/publication through four fixed coupling sweeps; preserve documented one-way/two-way semantics, reciprocal exchange, physical accuracy limits and atomic overflow/failure recovery. No per-edge index, routine host readback/global wait, silent truncation or second timestep is permitted.

Run installed public-API interaction fixtures and actual native work counters on an applicable physical GPU, preserving inputs and quality oracles. Build all applicable adapters; F8-56 and final device qualification retain full Gallery and physical platform obligations.
evidence: PASS: freshly installed public CUDA loader/driver coupling fixture on NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080; 467 dispatches, 530 workgroups, 37843 bytes, 628 barriers, 11 candidate dispatches, 259 coupling dispatches, one BVH build/publication; docs/roadmap/evidence/F8-55-shared-bvh-coupling-batching.json

PASS: D3D12 DXIL build, Metal generation, CUDA mirror and Vulkan SPIR-V mirror validation; docs/roadmap/evidence/F8-55-shared-bvh-coupling-batching.json
